entries.note: Originally taken at sealed opening on the premise that Arsenal missing Mosquera/Timber/Saliba was 'a genuine defensive crisis.' Owner caught the error, not the process: Arsenal are 6 wins from 6 in all competitions this season, including matches missing this exact back-three combination -- Saliba out long-term since before the season got going, Timber already out for most of those wins, Mosquera's 3-game absence also during the winning run. Old, already-priced-in news was treated as fresh and decision-relevant, without checking the team's actual results with the current lineup situation. Declined because the premise was wrong, independent of the price -- not adjusted to fit a smaller or larger edge. See collaboration/claude-input.json for the full correction and CLAUDE.md for the resulting standing process note (weigh recent form/results, not just an injury list in isolation).

entries.would_have_note: Recorded honestly per methodology section 9. This does not reopen the decision: the premise the pick rested on ('Arsenal missing three first-choice centre-backs, a defensive crisis') was factually wrong on the day -- only Saliba was absent; Timber and Mosquera both started. Brighton won for reasons unconnected to the stated reasoning. A bet winning for reasons other than why it was placed is the clearest possible illustration of why decision quality and outcome are scored separately here.
